hints: Remember one formula unit means one $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion plus one $\text{CN}^-$ ion, so count bonds in both ions separately.
Look at how $\text{NH}_3$ becomes $\text{NH}_4^+$, one $\text{N-H}$ bond must be formed using the lone pair on nitrogen.
Draw $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ in the cyanide ion and recall a triple bond is one sigma plus two pi, then add the counts together.
walkthrough:
**Split the ionic compound into its ions**

Think of $\text{NH}_4\text{CN}$ as two separate ions sitting together.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{CN}^-$$
This helps because coordinate bonds are in the cation and pi bonds are in the anion.

**Find the coordinate bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$**

In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen has three normal $\text{N-H}$ bonds plus one lone pair. That lone pair is donated to $\text{H}^+$ from $\text{HCN}$ to make the fourth $\text{N-H}$ bond.

A bond formed when one atom supplies both electrons is a coordinate (dative covalent) bond. So $\text{NH}_4^+$ contains 1 coordinate bond and 3 normal covalent bonds.

**Find the pi bonds in $\text{CN}^-$**

The cyanide ion is $[\text{C}\equiv\text{N}]^-$ with a triple bond between C and N.

$$\text{triple bond} = 1 \times \sigma + 2 \times \pi$$
So there are 2 pi bonds. There are no pi bonds in $\text{NH}_4^+$, which has only single bonds.

**Add up for one formula unit**

Coordinate bonds = 1 (from $\text{NH}_4^+$) + 0 (from $\text{CN}^-$) = 1.

Pi bonds = 0 (from $\text{NH}_4^+$) + 2 (from $\text{CN}^-$) = 2. That matches 1 coordinate bond and 2 pi bonds.

options.A: Incorrect. It correctly gives 2 pi bonds from the $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond, but says 0 coordinate bonds. It misses that the fourth $\text{N-H}$ bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$ is formed by donation of the nitrogen lone pair to $\text{H}^+$, which is a coordinate bond.
options.B: Correct. $\text{NH}_4^+$ contributes 1 coordinate bond from $\text{NH}_3$ donating its lone pair to $\text{H}^+$. $\text{CN}^-$ is $[\text{C}\equiv\text{N}]^-$ which has a triple bond, giving 2 pi bonds. Total is 1 coordinate and 2 pi.
options.C: Incorrect. It misses the coordinate bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$ and overcounts pi bonds. A common trap is to think a triple bond means 3 pi bonds, but a triple bond is 1 sigma plus only 2 pi bonds.
options.D: Incorrect. It correctly spots the 1 coordinate bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$, but says 3 pi bonds. This comes from confusing the total number of bonds in $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ (which is 3) with the number of pi bonds (which is 2).
